scenes.line: You hold a policy with Guardian Life. Your representative has moved on.
So here is the question. What happens if you choose not to have an agent at all?
Your policy does not need an agent to work.
Your premiums are collected. Your cover stays in force. A claim is still paid.
A note on your birthday. A reminder before a premium is due. A desk that answers the phone.
So what do you actually give up?
Nobody checks whether the cover you bought still fits the life you have now.
And nobody tells you what is already sitting inside it.

scenes.eyebrow: Things people find out too late
scenes.line: A benefit that pays your premiums if illness stops you working. A policy that has quietly matured. Money in one you thought had lapsed.
And if a payment stops, nobody notices until a letter arrives.
Your premium is priced on the age you were when you started.
Nobody can sell you that price again. Not us. Not anyone.

scenes.eyebrow: If anyone asks you to change it
scenes.line: So if someone asks you to replace this policy, the law is already on your side.

scenes.eyebrow: The Insurance Act of Trinidad and Tobago
scenes.line: No agent, broker or sales representative may have you replace a long term policy without first discussing the advantages and the disadvantages with you. Ask for that in writing.
That is what your own agent is for. Trained. Registered. Answerable for the advice they give.
So let us introduce you to yours. One click, and we do the rest.
Ricky Rampersad Branch. Guardian Life of the Caribbean.
